title: Reboxetine for acute treatment of major depression: systematic review and meta-analysis of published and unpublished placebo and selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor controlled trials
authors: Eyding D, Lelgemann M, Grouven U, Härter M, Kromp M, Kaiser T, et al.
population: Adults with major depressive disorder in 13 double-blind acute treatment trials of reboxetine versus placebo or SSRIs
funder: This work was supported by IQWiG. The original health technology assessment report was commissioned by the German Federal Joint Committee.
authorConflicts: No support from any company for the submitted work. Eyding was employed by H Lundbeck A/S from January 2006 to April 2007; Härter received remuneration from Boehringer Ingelheim and Lilly Pharma for three talks in 2008; five authors were IQWiG employees.
result: Data on 3033 of 4098 patients (74%) were unpublished and were obtained as clinical study reports from the manufacturer. With these data, remission did not differ from placebo (OR 1.17, 95% CI 0.91 to 1.51) and was less frequent than with SSRIs (OR 0.80, 0.67 to 0.96). Published data overestimated benefit versus placebo by up to 115% and versus SSRIs by up to 23%. All trials were sponsored by predecessors of Pfizer, except one sponsored by Lundbeck.
